 Mr. Amal Kumar Sen,
 Ms. Sahina Sumi
 ...for the respondent nos. 4, 7 to 12.
Ms. Manika Roy ...for the Nhai.
Affidavit-of-service filed in Court today be kept with the record.

Though Union of India and the competent authority under the National Highways Act, 1956 are arraigned as respondent nos. 1 and 8, they do not have any role in the instant writ petition, and,
therefore, their names from the array of respondents be expunged.

It is the case of the petitioner that petitioner's land with structure (hereinafter described as the subject land) was acquired by the competent authority under the State Highways Act for construction of a bypass connecting NH 81 from Chanchal to NH 81.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner was compelled to move the arbitrator for enhancement of the land.
It was enhanced by the arbitrator.
However, the enhanced money has not been paid to the petitioner.
The copy of the award has also not been served to the petitioner.

The learned Advocate for the petitioner also submits that under the provision of Section 38 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 no acquisition of the land is before payment of compensation as well as rehabilitation and resettlement, entitlements are paid or tendered to the entitled persons.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the petitioner is not only entitled to get compensation for the land which is intended to be possessed but he is also entitled to compensation for the structure which has eventually been lost due to such acquisition.

As per second schedule of 2013 Act the petitioner is entitled to get an alternative house,
land for land, if the land in question is under development, cost of development of the land, choice of entitlement and infrastructural amenities as provided in the third schedule of 2013 Act.
The said entitlement of the petitioner is beyond the scope of determination of compensation by the arbitrator under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act.

Until and unless such relief is granted to the petitioner the Collector cannot acquire the land and hand it over to the requiring body, i.e., PWD,
National Highway Division.
Mr. Sen, learned Advocate for the State respondent has submitted the statement of fact regarding computation of compensation in respect of the land and structure of the petitioner.

It is found from the said report that the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 was duly considered and amount of compensation was fixed by the Collector for the land and structure.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner was dissatisfied and moved for arbitration.
Arbitrator enhanced the award for land and structure.
The State respondents are in the process of payment of such compensation and award.
Thus, it is submitted from the statement of fact that total compensation has not been paid to the petitioner as yet.

Secondly, petitioner has not been granted the relief for rehabilitation and Adarsh Kumar Ram vs Union Of India & Ors on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5111168/
2 resettlement as per schedule 2 and 3 of 2013 Act.

entities.text: Adarsh Kumar Ram vs Union Of India & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Determination of compensation in respect of schedule 2 and schedule 3 is not within the jurisdiction of the arbitrator.
In view of such circumstances, this Court holds that the instant writ petition is prima facie maintainable.
The instant writ petition shall be disposed of on exchange of affidavits.

Therefore, the State respondents are directed to file affidavit-in-opposition within two weeks after vacation and serve a copy of the same to the learned Advocate-on-record on behalf of the petitioner.
The petitioner is at liberty to file affidavit-in-reply, if any, within ten days from the date of receipt of the affidavit-in-opposition.
The instant writ petition shall be listed in the Combined Monthly List of December, 2023.

Since Section 38 of 2013 Act creates a bar against taking possession of the acquired land before payment of entire compensation amount, if the land in question is in possession of the petitioner as on this date, status quo in respect of such possession shall be maintained by both the parties till 15 th December, 2023.

(Bibek Chaudhuri, J.)
